question.questionText: I wanted to talk to Shirley. Unfortunately, she ____________.
question.explanationHtml:
Detailed Explanation:
The sentence 'I wanted to talk to Shirley. Unfortunately, she ____________.' describes a past situation where the speaker wanted to talk to Shirley, but something had already happened before that moment. In this context, we need to use the past perfect tense to show that Shirley left before the speaker wanted to talk to her.
  • had already left (verb phrase (past perfect)): Past perfect tense, used to indicate an action that happened before another action in the past.
  • has already left (verb phrase (present perfect)): Present perfect tense, used to indicate an action that happened at an unspecified time before now.
  • left (verb (simple past)): Simple past tense, used to indicate an action that happened at a specific time in the past.
Related structure or vocabulary: Past perfect tense: had + past participle. Used to show that one action happened before another action in the past.
